item.title: Rotating Black Holes in Perfect Fluid Dark Matter: Horizons, Photon Orbits, and Shadows
item.description: arXiv:2611.08520v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate rotating black holes surrounded by perfect-fluid dark matter (PFDM), described by the parameter \(k\), and determine the Kerr-connected region of the \((a/M,k/M)\) parameter space that contains an event horizon. The critical value \(k_{\mathrm c}(a)\), obtained from the degenerate-horizon conditions \(\Delta(r_{\mathrm c})=\Delta'(r_{\mathrm c})=0\), defines the boundary between black-hole and horizonless configurations. We derive an exact parametric form of this extremal boundary and show that its near-Kerr behavior includes a logarithmic correction; therefore, \(k_{\mathrm c}/M\simeq2.8828(1-a/M)^{1.5377}\) is only an empirical fit over \(0.90\leq a/M\leq0.999\), not an asymptotic scaling law. For horizon-bearing solutions, we calculate unstable spherical photon orbits and the shadow's mean radius, area, and distortion, finding that increasing \(k/M\) shifts the photon region inward and reduces the shadow size. Backward ray tracing through a phenomenological optically thin disk, tested on independent \(41^2\), \(81^2\), and \(161^2\) image grids, confirms this trend: for \(a/M=0.9\) and an inclination of \(17^\circ\), the \(20~\mu\mathrm{as}\) beam-convolved ridge diameter decreases from \(42.47\) to \(37.88~\mu\mathrm{as}\) as \(k/M\) increases from 0 to \(0.08\), with the two finest grids agreeing to within \(0.5\%\). Thus, PFDM produces a consistent contraction from the horizon and photon region to the geometric shadow and image ridge, although these illustrative images do not provide an Event Horizon Telescope constraint because they lack a self-consistent emission model and interferometric likelihood analysis.
item.dc:creator: G. G. L. Nashed

item.title: How balloons lose their charge by collecting ions from the air
item.description: arXiv:2611.08521v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The air we breathe contains radioactive particles. Each time one of these particles decays, it creates hundreds of thousands of ionized air molecules. These ions make the air conductive, which is one reason insulated surfaces lose charge over time. Here we observe the discharge of two statically charged balloons by measuring the repulsive force between them over time. The initial rates of charge loss are relatively large, especially at higher humidities. This large rate of charge loss is likely dominated by the emission of water ions from the balloons surface. Approximately 1 hour after charging, the charge loss rates are much smaller and agree with predictions calculated from the radon concentration in the air and the size of the room, for reasonable aerosol concentrations.
item.dc:creator: J. Pantaleone (University of Alaska Anchorage)

item.title: $\cal{PT}$-Symmetric GUP-Modified Single- and Double-Well Quartic Oscillators
item.description: arXiv:2611.08530v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the GUP-deformed quartic oscillator $H_\eta=p^2+\eta p^4+x^4$ and distinguish its real-axis realization from complex-contour realizations. A contour chosen to remain in the decay sectors compatible with the undeformed quartic oscillator gives low-lying eigenvalues that approach the ordinary quartic spectrum as $\eta\to0^+$. This limiting-compatible contour does not, by itself, produce a low-level $\PT$-symmetry-breaking transition. To investigate exceptional points while retaining the same quartic leading behavior, we then introduce the explicitly $\PT$-symmetric extension $H_{\eta,a,g}=p^2+\eta p^4+x^4-a x^2+\ii g x^3$ and fix $a=4$, for which the real part of the potential has a double-well form. Harmonic-oscillator-basis diagonalization with basis dimensions up to $N=100$ yields a converged exceptional-point branch: the critical coupling increases from $g_{\mathrm{EP}}\simeq0.10222364$ at $\eta=0$ to $g_{\mathrm{EP}}\simeq0.15603309$ at $\eta=0.1$. Across the transition, the two lowest real eigenvalues coalesce and continue as a complex-conjugate pair. The exceptional-point results belong to this stated double-well extension, not to the original single-well Hamiltonian alone.
item.dc:creator: Saber Zarrinkamar

item.title: Jacobi's principle of stationary full action and its implications
item.description: arXiv:2512.17944v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The purpose of this article is to extend the applicability of the principle of stationary Jacobi action to non-conservative natural systems and to derive the equations of motion corresponding to this generalized principle. To this end, in addition to the well-known variation of the Jacobi action with respect to coordinates, we introduce an independent variation of time. Small variations in both coordinates and time are considered at points along the actual trajectory, subject to standard boundary conditions.
